intent_en: To explain how the yield curve (interest rates across different time horizons) serves as a tool for predicting economic downturns by reflecting market expectations.
previous_intent: To explain how interest rates across different time periods reflect market expectations of economic direction and help predict economic downturns.
narration_support: when you're trying to predict a downturn, you're often trying to get a read on people's expectations of where the economy is heading. Which is why that curve is so useful.
chart_support: Line chart plotting interest rates against time (from 3m to 10y) for Q2 2019, illustrating the yield curve shape.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly links the 'curve' to predicting downturns and expectations. The chart visualizes this curve as interest rates over time (3m vs 10y), which is the standard representation of a yield curve used for such predictions.
